cands.name: Alan Thomas

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Birmingham native and self-described entrepreneur who ran as a Democrat for Alabama House District 50 in 2026. He says he has worked at Children's of Alabama, in the service industry, and in investigative journalism and policy research. He has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no independent news coverage of Alan Thomas, so his background rests on his own campaign site and Ballotpedia survey. We could not confirm his employers, the details of his business, or his claim that he advised current legislators. We could not confirm that he attended graduate school at UNC Chapel Hill. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He has never held office, so there is no record of official actions.

local.label: Roots 100: Thomas says on his campaign site and in his Ballotpedia survey that he was born and raised in Birmingham and attended The Altamont School there; both sources are his own statements. · Money: 8% of money from District 50 ZIP codes

qual.background: Ballotpedia lists his profession as entrepreneur. He says he worked at Children's of Alabama and in the service industry, and did investigative journalism and policy research that he says supported and advised current legislators. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: He has a self-reported business and work background but no legislative or elected experience. The policy-research and legislator-advising claims are his own and I could not verify them, so he is placed in the middle range for business owners and the self-employed.

cands.name: Bill Morris

top: Alabama Voice Of Teachers For Education (a-vote)
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican from St. Clair County. Former Mayor of Moody (1992–2003) and General Manager of Leeds Water Works. Member of the St. Clair County Board of Education and appointee to the Central Alabama Water Board. Won the 2026 Republican primary for Alabama House District 50.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from Morris on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. His campaign site names workforce development and education as priorities but gives no detail on teacher pay or vouchers. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no documented controversies, and no records of his actions or votes as mayor, school board member or water board member. His birthplace and the year he began living in Alabama are not stated in the pages we had. The dates of his school board service and his water utility role are not given either.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site describes him as a lifelong resident of St. Clair County, and he was Mayor of Moody starting in 1992; his birthplace is not stated, and the residency claim comes from his own campaign. · Money: 8% of money from District 50 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (9% before)
